actionable_steps.citation: Imbibe Bhaarath's ideals — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 27 (1994), 1994-02-03
actionable_steps.step: Begin with Vakmounam — confine your speech to the limit and the needs of the occasion; avoid excessive talk.

actionable_steps.citation: Imbibe Bhaarath's ideals — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 27 (1994), 1994-02-03
actionable_steps.step: Move to Mano-mounam — reduce the bundle of thoughts gradually, like unwinding a clock, until the mind comes under control.

actionable_steps.citation: Experience Divinity Within In Total Silence — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 37 (2004), 2004-11-22
actionable_steps.step: Turn your vision inward and observe absolute silence daily — only then can you realise the all-pervasive divinity.

actionable_steps.citation: Education For Supreme Bliss — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 33 (2000), 2000-11-22
actionable_steps.step: Guard the tongue against its four errors: uttering falsehood, scandalising, finding fault with others, and excessive speech.
Train the mind to keep quiet — don't let it run after this and that; keep the mental reactions to the outer world far away.

definition.citation: Discipline is the Life Principle of Man (Alternative Translation) — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 29 (1996), 1996-06-19
definition.quote: It is said that silence is God (Nisshabdam Brahma). In fact, the sound that is there in silence is Brahman.

discourses.citation: Education For Supreme Bliss — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 33 (2000), 2000-11-22
discourses.quote: Silence is the only language of the realised. Practice moderation in speech. That will help you in many ways. It will develop Prema, for most misunderstandings and factions arise out of carelessly spoken words.

discourses.citation: Experience Divinity Within In Total Silence — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 37 (2004), 2004-11-22
discourses.quote: Turn your vision inward and observe absolute silence. Only then can you realise the all-pervasive divinity. … You can experience divine bliss only in absolute silence.

discourses.citation: Imbibe Bhaarath's ideals — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 27 (1994), 1994-02-03
discourses.quote: "Less speech, more happiness." The ancients practised three kinds of silent penance to control speech. The first was Vakmounam (silence of the tongue), the second one was Mano-mounam (silence of the mind) and the third was Maha-mounam (Supreme Silence).

discourses.citation: Pay the price — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 5 (1965), 1965-09-30
discourses.quote: Silence is the best sadhana, to guard faith.

make_it_real: Speech is silver, silence is golden — try one hour of chosen silence today and hear what your heart has been trying to say.
title: Silence

vahinis.quote: "Practice silence (mounam bhajasva)," it is said. But what is silence? Not simply keeping the mouth shut. It means getting beyond the influence of all the senses and getting established always in the consciousness of one's own reality.
